result:
I graded s2 for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`: three correct, two partial, one wrong. The file is a copy of the draft I read back earlier, but I didn't re-read it after writing it. The check command I tried needed approval, so I read the draft by eye and didn't run a JSON validator.

| Item | Verdict | Misconception | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | none | An agent is a loop of actions and results. |
| q2 | correct | none | The model outputs a tool request. |
| q3 | wrong | M6 | You chose "let it run longer". A stuck agent needs a step limit. |
| q4 | partial | M4 | Your 4 is right, but the model doesn't run the tools itself. The program does. |
| q5 | correct | none | The result goes back in as the model's next input. |
| q6 | partial | none | You said the model picks a tool by its name. It also reads each tool's description. |

I kept q4 as partial even though the number is right. Your stated reason (the model runs the tools itself) is wrong, and the grading rules count that as partial.

The reviewer ran twice. After the first pass I shortened the q4 and q6 feedback and fixed the summary so it no longer points to a lesson file that doesn't exist. The second pass suggested trimming q3 and loosening the summary tone. I didn't apply those because the two-pass limit was reached. Those findings are in `review-records/0001-s2-grade.md`.

I also added learning record `0003-agent-loop-quiz-and-two-gaps.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. s1 is still ungraded.

**Next step:** reread `learning-records/0002-the-agent-loop.md`. Then write out one run of the loop in two columns, "model outputs" and "program does", and mark where a step limit would stop it.
